item.title: Belgian farmer hasn't irrigated crops in 26 years; soil remains moist just 5-10 cm below surface
item.description: Belgium’s Diederik Steyaert has successfully farmed without irrigation for over two decades. His dedication to organic practices ensures that the soil remains healthy and retains moisture efficiently. By eliminating ploughing and incorporating organic matter, Steyaert cultivates robust plants that adapt to stress and drought. This innovative approach showcases vital strategies for addressing agricultural challenges in water-limited environments.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2017, wildfire neared Roslyn; 9 years later, the town burned 500+ acres to prevent future fires
item.description: Washington communities are increasingly implementing prescribed burns as a strategy to mitigate wildfire risks. By imitating natural fire cycles, this method effectively decreases fuel accumulation. Roslyn, a town previously devastated by a wildfire, has embraced this practice extensively, fostering collaboration among various agencies and private landowners. This innovative strategy provides a fresh perspective on coexisting with wildfire threats.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: After 45 months of observation, capuchins increasingly hunted small animals when fruit became scarce
item.description: In Brazil, capuchin monkeys exhibit remarkable adaptability by hunting small animals when fruit supplies dwindle. This shift highlights their versatile omnivorous diet and responsiveness to environmental changes. Interestingly, adult males were observed hunting vertebrates more often than younger females. Furthermore, when alternative food sources were available, the monkeys relied less on hunting, presenting intriguing implications for understanding the dietary evolution of early human ancestors.

item.title: Two vacant Connecticut office buildings will become 286 apartments in a $120 million conversion, reusing 511,000 sq ft instead of tearing them down
item.description: Transforming the urban landscape, two idle office buildings in Connecticut are set to be revitalized into vibrant apartments. With a projected budget of $120 million backed by Bank OZK, this redevelopment will introduce 286 loft-style residential units, complete with modern facilities. The project emphasizes the importance of reusing existing properties, offering excellent rail connectivity to surrounding urban centers and major thoroughfares.

item.title: An Oklahoma woman opened a $1,373 electric bill, including a $598 deposit after late payments
item.description: As intense summer heat sweeps through the region, many households are grappling with skyrocketing electricity bills. Raelynn McMurchy's monthly statement doubled, igniting discussions on much-needed policy reforms. Oklahoma's power provider continues to disconnect customers in alarming numbers, leaving local charities to struggle for emergency support. Residents are calling for robust measures to prevent power shutoffs during the scorching months.

item.title: In 2020, Albany brought 1,500 feet of Patroon Creek back above ground after decades in a pipe
item.description: Engineers in Albany revitalized Patroon Creek by daylighting it, restoring its natural flow and creating vital green spaces. This innovative project significantly bolstered flood protection for surrounding neighborhoods. Post-restoration water monitoring assured that the creek effectively managed heavy rains, tackling water quality concerns while promoting a healthier aquatic ecosystem. The initiative not only enhances the environment but also provides recreational opportunities for the local community.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: An Ohio couple spent 30 years in the country for pieces of an amusement park that closed in 1984
item.description: Completion of the exterior work at Youngstown's Idora Park museum marks a significant milestone, with the Mahoning Valley Historical Society now moving forward into the interior design stage. The museum is dedicated to exhibiting a diverse collection of park artifacts collected through the years. Fundraising initiatives are actively underway to support the project's financial objectives, reinforcing the museum's mission to honor and convey Youngstown's vibrant cultural history.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2021, Pennsylvania removed a 128-year-old dam; Sterry Creek’s original channel was still intact
item.description: The Nature Conservancy has successfully revitalized the O'Conner Reservoir dam from the late 1800s, allowing Sterry Creek to revert to its natural course. By lowering the reservoir's water levels and excavating the embankment, they eliminated the need for a costly artificial channel, thus improving local water health. This project also established a natural floodplain and reconnected important stream habitats to the expansive Lackawanna River watershed.

item.title: A London apartment burned down in 2024 and left more than 80 people homeless
item.description: Residents of London are still obligated to pay mortgages on homes that were ruined by fire, despite the complexities in the ongoing legal struggles involving insurers and administrators. The building's freeholder has gone into administration following the destruction. Consequently, residents are stuck facing demands for unpaid service charges relative to properties that no longer exist, intensifying pressure on the government regarding building safety and restitution for the affected individuals.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1776, a Gettysburg minister built his stone home; 200 years later a young couple saved it from...
item.description: Celebrating its 250th anniversary, Gettysburg's historic Dobbin House hosted a memorable consecration ceremony. Originally completed in 1776, this iconic building has played various roles over the centuries. In the 1970s, local patrons Jacqueline and Gary White saved it from being demolished. The upcoming unveiling of Dobbin House Square promises new museum exhibits. The anniversary festivities will include reenactments, enchanting music, and a ceremonial cannon salute.
